title: Police Issue Traffic and Safety Advisories for Deepavali in Little India
text: Police Issue Traffic and Safety Advisories for Deepavali in Little India Authorities have announced traffic restrictions, including the closure of the Birch Road crossing, and banned public drinking and fireworks in Little India and Geylang to manage heavy crowds and ensure safety during the Deepavali festival celebrations. Auxiliary police officers will be present, alongside directional signboards, to manage movements and provide assistance. Set as preferred sourceHeavy crowds are expected in Little India for Deepavali, especially on the eve of the Hindu festival on Nov 7. Police advise using alternative routes and staying alert for safety. Birch Road crossing will close from 4pm on Nov 7 to 4am the next day. Campbell Lane may also close if needed, with nearby crossings available. Public drinking is banned in Little India and Geylang from Nov 6 to Nov 10.Police also warned against illegal fireworks and sparkler misuse, with strict penalties. The police said that heavy foot and vehicular traffic is expected along Serangoon Road during this period, urging motorists in a Nov 6 advisory to use alternative routes. The pedestrian crossing in Birch Road, in front of Anguilla Mosque, will shut from 4pm on Nov 7 till 4am the next day, the police said.The pedestrian crossing at Campbell Lane may also be closed if required, with alternative crossings available near Sungei Road or near Dunlop Street. These closures are to ensure crowd and traffic management for the safety of pedestrians and road users, said the police. Auxiliary police officers will be on the ground alongside directional signboards to manage movements and provide assistance.The public is advised to stay vigilant and look after their belongings by slinging bags across their fronts, keeping them zipped and not leaving wallets in back pockets. – from 10.30pm on Nov 6 to 7am on Nov 10. First-time offenders found afoul of the law face fines of up to $1,500. Repeat offenders may be fined up to $3,000 or jailed for up to 4½ months, or both.Retailers who are caught selling alcohol beyond permitted trading hours risk losing their liquor licences, the police said.“Such illegal discharge of fireworks poses danger to the public and their properties,” said the authorities. “The police will take strict enforcement action against offenders who possess, discharge or import fireworks illegally. In 2025, a total of 45 people were investigated for offences related to the possession, discharge and importation of fireworks, which are classified as explosives.Fireworks-related offences can result in a jail term of up to three years and a fine of up to $50,000 for individuals, or $100,000 for entities. Misusing sparklers, such as by bundling them together and setting them off at once, is also illegal and poses a potential fire hazard, said the police. Those found guilty of the offence can be jailed for up to a year or fined up to $5,000, or both.Those who end up hurting someone else while misusing sparklers can be jailed for up to three years or fined, or both.
